Founded in 1927, this museum houses a library and museum with displays illustrating the development and grammar of the modern invented language Esperanto.

Vienna's mainstream everyday gay disco. The crowd is varied. It is in the 1st District at Tiefer Graben 22 (Herrengasse U3). Saturdays are house music free.
A gay resource center with an excellent bar and restaurant. (Pilgramgasse U4)
A very authentic and chic napolitanian pizza parlor. Large, delicious pizzas and a range of Italian food. The wine card has interesting Austrian white wine choices.
Vegan and vegetarian café serving good food. One can choose between interesting regional and international beers and wines.

Decent Austro-Mex food, but come for the cocktails.

Serves classic Viennese cuisine.
A very low-key, classy yuppie restaurant.
Large beer garden, some say they have the best beer in Vienna and they also offer traditional Austrian dishes at moderate prices. Also well-known for its excellent Stelze (knuckle of pork).
Austria's largest club. Come dressed like euro-trash to get in. Thursday is ladies' night with free entry and drinks. Popular with the young conservative working class.
A small bar with a DJ and dance floor. It is a very local place and the crowd is an array of people of all ages from the neighborhood.
An upstairs bar and its downstairs club-like half Fluc Wanne (meaning tub). Most of the club is underground in a former underpass, so do not miss it. More alternative with very diverse DJs and bands.

This Vienna Heurigen serves both excellent wines, native juices, Murauer beer and cold specialities from the Schneeberg or Carinthian Gailtal.

Good schnitzel, potatoes and pork. The food is very good, different from what you can eat in typical Austrian restaurants. Cool atmosphere.
Fast food versions of local food. Not bad if you are on a budget and do not have much time to spare.
Recommendation if you are looking for home-style, local food. The atmosphere is cozy. The service provides competent and friendly advice.

Authentic local fast food. Very good meatloaf and other convenient Vienna traditional light meals.
Legendary stall at Hoher Markt. As always great sausages.
Great sausage. The seller can explain everything about all types of sausages.
A lovely spot for street meat. Good flavors and great/friendly service.

Famous for Wienerschnitzel. They claim to have the biggest schnitzel in the world. If you are not really hungry, one may easily be enough for two people (just ask for a second plate). Traditionally, you would want a potato salad with that.

eat.h: Mon-Fri from 08:00, Sat Sun and holidays from 10:00

A bourgeois Viennese restaurant offering good seasonal local food. In summertime you can sit outdoors.
An Italian place serving good mostly authentic Italian food.
The Vietnamese restaurant offers lots of vegetarian choices. Their vegetables are well prepared using good herbs combinations.
Part of a local chain. Informal and popular place serving generic but reasonably priced Japanese and Korean dishes. The menu has a vegetarian section. Quick service by efficient waiters.
Belongs to a famous winery Artner. It offers creative, fresh fare that tends to be on the lighter side than most Austrian cuisine. Excellent wine cellar, reservations recommended.
The restaurant since 25 years serves excellent food with Viennese charme and a big wine choice. It has one Michelin star.
The big lunch room in the Hotel Bristol reopened with the original art déco chandeliers and decorated ceiling. The restaurant may serve as elegant after Opera dinner.
Sushi bar popular with business travellers. Serves fresh and tasty fish that comes at a high price.
Italian fish restaurant combined with bar/lounge for Vienna's glitterati. Quality is excellent.
The gourmet restaurant is handled by 2 Michelin-starred chef Silvio Nickol. It offers a 5-, 7- or 9-course menu. The seasonal wine card is exquisite.

A very nice restaurant that specialises in beef (claimed to be only local and from trusted farmers) and has some flavour of traditional Austrian cuisine. Try the Tafelspitz, it comes in a copper pan and still is in the soup it was…
Excellent northern Italian fare with a range of fine specialties. Slightly small portions but an extensive wine list to drown this particular sorrow in. Reservations recommended.

Star chef Paul Ivić from Tyrol leads one of only two vegetarian Michelin-starred restaurants in Europe, with an excellent wine selection. Occasionally he also offers workshops. Reservations can be made online or by phone.

The Japanese cook Hiroshi Sakai once governed this place that serves authentic Japanese food. One dines on the top floor of a splendid Viennese palace, that is nowadays the Grand Hotel. It has an excellent choice of special wines. The…
Viennese bourgeois restaurant cooked by Christian Domschitz.
The restaurant offers a menu with freshly cooked organic ingredients – from the classic Wiener Schnitzel to Chocolate-Almond-Cake without flour and Bio-Fruit-Ice-Cream.
Maybe the most popular place. You can choose from a lot of different flavors, but it's always crowded and you often have to stand in a queue for a few minutes.
Another excellent and popular ice cream parlour. Ask for the Special Nougat ice cream.

The Italian ice cream shop produces on the spot their own with exquisite ingredients like piemontese hazelnuts, caramelised pine nuts or fresh fruits.
In the same district as Eissalon. Popular with Viennese and tourists for its huge €2 cones to go.
Thomas Bernhard used to come here daily as do many other Viennese literate. It exists since more than 35 years. Happily expect Viennese grumpy senior waiters.

One of the most famous Vienna coffee houses, which opened in 1876, has been authentically restored. Beautiful premises inside the Palais Ferstel, it is too touristy and a bit more expensive for having a meal, but can be worth it for a…
Famous traditional coffeehouse, and equally good place for having a meal. They opened a second branch on Fleischmarkt.
This traditional café already existed at the times of Mozart and Beethoven. It serves Viennese food.
A very traditional Viennese café, hence visitors take their time to enjoy the lovely cakes.

Beautiful traditional Viennese café with view on the Schwarzenbergplatz and the Ring avenue. It has fine pastries and coffee choices.
Quaint, traditional café with art deco accents. Established in 1900.

A very traditional small Viennese café, opened at the end of the 19th century by Josef and Josefine Sluka, serves excellent pastries and bread. To the breakfast you can order oeuf poché. The choice on the menu is adjusted according…

Intergenerational café run as a social business: the cakes are baked by senior citizens to their own family recipes and served in a vintage living-room setting. Vegetarian lunch menu on weekdays, shaded outdoor seating in summer,…

This cafe/restaurant/bar is on a very medieval-looking lane in the central district and is a time warp of another kind: its folky-bohemian atmosphere could convince you that you're in North Beach or Greenwich Village, circa 1967.…
Special establishment where the time stood still.
The bar serves classical cocktails.
